headline: Massachusetts secures $153 million for 16 transportation projects
dek: The redistributed federal funds will support roads, bridges, shared-use paths and MBTA work, including a battery-electric rail layover facility in Boston.
body: Massachusetts has secured $153 million in additional federal transportation funding for 16 MassDOT and MBTA projects across the state, Gov. Maura Healey announced Thursday.

The money comes through the Federal Highway Administration's annual redistribution process, which makes federal dollars available when other states or programs cannot use them before the end of the federal fiscal year. Massachusetts had eligible projects ready to advance, the administration said.

The MassDOT projects include a $10.7 million corridor improvement on Shank Painter Road in Provincetown, a $23.44 million first phase of the Belmont Community Path, replacement of two Southbridge bridges and intersection improvements in Medford. Other awards will fund work in communities including Marion, Braintree, Brockton, Shrewsbury, Northborough and Holyoke.

MBTA awards include $32.64 million for the Widett Layover Facility in Boston, a regional-rail storage and maintenance site designed to support battery-electric trains; $15 million for an accessible Newtonville commuter-rail station; and $5.36 million for Fairmount Line infrastructure tied to planned decarbonized service. The projects are intended to stretch state transportation resources while improving roads, bridges, walking and biking connections and public transit.
